name: write_files
title: LixRay: Write files
description:
Create or update files in one atomic commit, parent directories included. Each file takes content as { text } or { base64 } and, optionally, lixcol_metadata (omitted keeps it, an object replaces it, null clears it); metadata alone updates an existing file. With last_seen_commit_id, a file that changed since that commit refuses the whole write: the error carries current_commit_id and the current content of the conflicting files, so merge and write again; unrelated changes never block. checkpoint: true marks the resulting commit. A successful write is already saved; read back if its outcome is uncertain or validation is requested. A write to a file LixRay can render (Markdown, CSV) returns the change as a card the reader can see, so describe the edit in a sentence rather than repeating the diff. Rename, delete, and everything else: execute_sql on lix_file and lix_directory.

name: query_sql
title: LixRay: Query SQL
description:
Run one read-only SQL statement against lix_ref (@handle/slug or UUID), optionally branch_id. Defaults to the repository default branch; no open_lix needed. Or pass context alone for its pinned branch. INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE are rejected; use execute_sql for writes.

Read repository data and files with SQL; read_files and list_files are optional conveniences. Lix SQL is a Postgres dialect subset, not SQLite: there is no sqlite_master and no PRAGMA. Discover tables with `SELECT table_name, table_type FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema = 'public' ORDER BY table_name;` and columns, with their descriptions, with `SELECT column_name, data_type, is_nullable, description FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name = $1 ORDER BY ordinal_position;`. Core tables: lix_file (id, path, directory_id, name, content), lix_directory (id, path, parent_id, name), lix_branch, lix_commit, lix_change; entity tables are repository-defined, so discover them rather than guess. Parameters are $1, $2, … given as params: [{ kind: "text", value: "…" }] (kinds: text, int, float, json, blob); file bytes read as CAST(content AS TEXT). History: lix_log() lists retained commits, lix_history('lix_file') the net change per commit, lix_diff('lix_file') the working changes, lix_as_of('lix_file', $1) the state at a commit.

name: execute_sql
title: Execute SQL atomically
description:
Run an ordered atomic SQL batch against lix_ref (@handle/slug or UUID), optionally branch_id. Defaults to the repository default branch; no open_lix needed. Or pass context alone for its pinned branch. If any statement fails, the complete batch is rolled back; a returned result is already persisted.

For text files use UPDATE lix_file SET content = CAST($1 AS BYTEA) WHERE path = $2 with two kind: "text" parameters (content, path). REPLACE, CONCAT and || can be used inside the BYTEA cast. Use one SQL statement per statements[] entry; use an explicit ON CONFLICT (path) target. write_files is an optional convenience. Rename with `UPDATE lix_file SET path = $1 WHERE path = $2`; delete with `DELETE FROM lix_file WHERE path = $1`; directories likewise on lix_directory (paths have no trailing slash: /skills, not /skills/). Lix supports `INSERT … ON CONFLICT (cols) DO UPDATE SET col = excluded.col` and DO NOTHING; ON CONSTRAINT and DO UPDATE WHERE are not supported; text bound for a byte column is written as `CAST($n AS BYTEA)`. Successful writes are persisted; read back only when the outcome is unknown or validation is part of the task. Errors identify a zero-based statement_index when available and report outcome as not_committed, unknown, or committed. Never blindly retry an unknown or committed outcome. Mark meaningful milestones with create_checkpoint; saving needs no checkpoint.

description:

Abandoned commits are kept until garbage collection; other branches are unchanged. create_checkpoint returns a usable commit_id; there is no restore_checkpoint tool.
